transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, what brings me in is that my sleep has just gotten really messed up lately. I'll either... I don't know, I'll stay up half the night with my mind just running, or I end up waking up way too early and feeling like I never even rested. It's just really starting to become a problem.
Have you had times when you slept much less than usual but still felt unusually energetic and did not feel tired?

Yeah, actually. Um, there were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, but I didn't feel tired at all. I still got up feeling completely charged... like, coffee wasn't even necessary to get going.
During those periods of sleeping very little, did you also feel unusually elevated or irritable compared with your normal mood?

Yeah, both, actually. Um... earlier in the month, I felt almost lit up, I guess? Just completely unstoppable. But then I'd also get really irritable. Like, I’d snap at my mom, or even my supervisor at work over just little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me at all.
How long did that unusually energized or irritable period last?

Um, I'm not entirely sure exactly how many days it was. It felt like it went on for a while, but I didn't really keep track of the exact dates or anything. It was just... a stretch of time where I felt like that.
Did that energized or irritable period last for at least four days in a row?

Um, I'm honestly just not sure. It might have been four days, or maybe just three... I really didn't track it. It definitely felt like a solid block of time, but I just can't say for certain if it was exactly four days in a row.
During that energized or irritable period, did it significantly interfere with your ability to function at work?

Well, I'm still showing up to work... but, um, I've been making some mistakes. Like, enough reconciliation errors that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to talk about it. So it's definitely affecting things there. And outside of work, I've just been avoiding my salsa class and not really seeing my friends because... I don't know, I just really don't feel like myself right now.
Did you ever need to be hospitalized because of that unusually energized or irritable period?
No, I haven't. I've never had to go to the hospital or anything like that for feeling that way. It really didn't get to that point.
Has there ever been a period of feeling unusually energized or irritable that lasted a full week or longer?
No, definitely not a full week. Like I said, it was maybe three or four days tops. It never lasted that long.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. It's been going on for at least that long. Lately I just wake up with this... this heavy, empty feeling. It's hard to explain, but like, even sitting in my own condo that I worked so hard for just makes me want to cry.
During this depressed period, have you lost interest in or pleasure from activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I stopped going to my salsa class completely. And my paints are still sitting out on the table, but... I don't know, I look at them and just feel nothing. It's like they belong to somebody else.

{"intent":"Assess for increased goal-directed activity during the elevated or irritable period as a symptom of hypomania","question":"During that energized or irritable period, did you take on noticeably more activities or projects than usual, or become much more goal-directed?"]

Yeah, I did actually. I just had so much energy... I started emailing a bunch of people about doing their books on the side, which I don't normally do. And I was mapping out all these different projects for my condo. I even started calling relatives to talk through all my plans, just way, way more than I usually would. It felt like I could get so much done all at once.
During this depressed period, have you felt unusually tired or lacking energy nearly every day?

Yeah, definitely. Um, even after getting a full night in bed, just... walking from the parking lot into the office feels like I’m dragging sandbags. And by the time lunch rolls around, my brain just feels completely worn out. It's like I have zero energy right now.
Thinking back, what was the longest uninterrupted stretch of days when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?

Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I didn't exactly keep track of the days when it was happening, so... I don't really know what the longest stretch was. It's hard to remember exactly how many days in a row it lasted.
Using any concrete events you remember as markers, was there one uninterrupted stretch of at least four consecutive days when you felt energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?

Um, I really can't say for sure. I know you're looking for a specific number of days, but even trying to think back to specific things that happened... it's all just kind of a blur. I don't know if it was four days in a row or not.
Did people close to you notice that you were distinctly more energized, talkative, or irritable than usual during that period?

Yeah, they did. My sister actually pointed it out to me. She told me I was talking so fast she couldn’t even get a word in. I guess I was just going on and on about equity, taxes, and then like... paint colors. And I could actually feel it myself, too—like I was just pushing myself to keep going and keep talking.
During that stretch of increased energy and irritability, did you return to your usual mood and energy at any point, even briefly, before the period ended?

Um... I honestly don't know. Like I was saying before, that whole time is just really blurry for me, so I don't remember if I had a normal day or even a normal afternoon in the middle of it all. I just remember the feeling of being so sped up, but I couldn't tell you if it paused or went back to normal at any point before it was completely over.
During that energized or irritable period, did you ever hear or see things that others could not, or believe things that others told you were not true?

No, nothing like that. Um, I never saw or heard anything that wasn't there. And I didn't have any weird beliefs that people had to correct me on or anything. I was just really sped up, like I said, but my mind wasn't playing tricks on me.
Can you identify any specific four consecutive calendar days during which you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?

I can't really point to a specific four days on a calendar, no. Like I said, it's all just a blur to me now. I know it lasted for a while, but I couldn't give you exact dates or say for sure it was exactly four days in a row.
Did your depressed period begin after the energized or irritable period ended?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um... like I mentioned, the timeline is pretty fuzzy for me. I know I had that time where I was really sped up, and I know I had the depression, but... I couldn't tell you for sure if the depression started right after the energized part ended. I just don't remember the exact order of how it all happened.
Have you ever had another clearly separate period when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little better or had a good day, but nothing like that one specific time where I was just totally wired and not sleeping. It was really just that one main period that stands out.

The symptom profiles provide duration for the depressive episode (5 months) and the cycling (1 month), but do not have a specific item detailing the exact sequence of when the depressed period began relative to the energized period ending.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a depressive period lasting at least two weeks with depressed mood, marked anhedonia, and prominent low energy causing occupational and social impairment. Although there were hypomanic-like symptoms including decreased need for sleep, increased energy, irritability, pressured speech, and increased goal-directed activity, the required duration of at least four consecutive days was not established, and there was no confirmed week-long episode, hospitalization, or psychosis. Therefore, an unspecified depressive disorder is the most supportable diagnosis pending further longitudinal clarification.

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed or empty mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks
Marked loss of interest or pleasure in salsa dancing and painting
Prominent fatigue and markedly reduced energy nearly every day
Difficulty sleeping, including staying awake much of the night and waking too early
Periods of sleeping only three to four hours without feeling tired
Decreased need for sleep during an energized period
Increased goal-directed activity and multiple new projects
Pressured or markedly increased speech noticed by the patient's sister
Increased occupational and interpersonal activity compared with usual

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Depressed mood and associated symptoms were present for at least two weeks. The duration of the energized or irritable period was not established as at least four consecutive days.
additional_requirements: Occupational impairment confirmed by reconciliation errors and supervisory concern
No hospitalization during the energized or irritable period
No energized or irritable episode lasting one week or longer was reported
